title.zh: 卷五十二 列傳第十二 庾悅 王誕 謝景仁 袁湛 褚叔度
title.en: Volume 52 Biographies 12: Yu Yue, Wang Dan, Xie Jingren, Yuan Zhan, Chu Shudu
title.raw: 卷五十二 列傳第十二 庾悅 王誕 謝景仁 袁湛 褚叔度 Volume 52 Biographies 12: Yu Yue, Wang Dan, Xie Jingren, Yuan Zhan, Chu Shudu

sentences.zh: 庾悅，字仲豫，潁川𨻳陵人也。

translations.literal: Yu Yue, courtesy name Zhongyu, was a native of Yancheng in Yingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yue, styled Zhongyu, came from Yancheng in Yingchuan Commandery.

sentences.zh: 曾祖亮，晉太尉。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Liang was Grand Commandant of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Liang had served as Jin Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 祖羲，吳國內史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Xi was Interior Minister of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Xi had been Interior Minister of Wu.

sentences.zh: 父准，西中郎將、豫州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Zhun was General of the Right in the Center and Inspector of Yu Province.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhun held the posts of General of the Right in the Center and Inspector of Yu Province.

sentences.zh: 悅少為衛將軍琅邪王行參軍、司馬，徙主簿，轉右長史。

translations.literal: In his youth Yue served as Acting Retainer and Major to the General of the Guard, the Prince of Langye, then was moved to Chief Clerk and transferred to Right Chief Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth Yue served the Prince of Langye as acting retainer and major under the General of the Guard, then became chief clerk and was promoted to right chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 桓玄輔政，領豫州，以悅為別駕從事史，遷驍騎將軍。

translations.literal: When Huan Xuan assisted in government and held Yu Province, he appointed Yue Administrative Aide and Attending Clerk, then promoted him to General of Valiant Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: When Huan Xuan held the regency and took charge of Yu Province, he made Yue his administrative aide and attending clerk, later promoting him to General of Valiant Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 玄篡位，徙中書侍郎。

translations.literal: When Xuan usurped the throne, Yue was moved to Gentleman Attendant of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: After Xuan seized the throne, Yue was transferred to Gentleman Attendant of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 高祖定京邑，武陵王遵承制，以悅為寧遠將軍、安遠護軍、武陵內史。

translations.literal: When the High Ancestor secured the capital region, the Prince of Wuling Zun, acting on imperial authority, appointed Yue General of Pacification at a Distance, Protector of the Army at a Distance, and Interior Minister of Wuling.
translations.idiomatic: After the High Ancestor took the capital, Prince Zun of Wuling, acting with imperial authority, made Yue General of Pacification at a Distance, Protector of the Army at a Distance, and Interior Minister of Wuling.

sentences.zh: 以病去職。

translations.literal: He left office on account of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned because of illness.

sentences.zh: 鎮軍府版諮議參軍，轉車騎從事中郎。

translations.literal: The Pacifying Army headquarters issued him a commission as Advising Retainer, and he was transferred to Attendant Gentleman of the Chariots and Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: The Pacifying Army headquarters commissioned him as advising retainer, after which he became attendant gentleman of the Chariots and Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 劉毅請為撫軍司馬，不就。

translations.literal: Liu Yi invited him to be Major of the Pacifying Army, but he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yi asked him to serve as major of the Pacifying Army, but he declined.

sentences.zh: 遷車騎中軍司馬。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Major of the Center Army under the Chariots and Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to major of the center army under the Chariots and Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 從征廣固，竭其誠力。

translations.literal: He followed the campaign against Guanggu and exhausted his loyal strength.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in the campaign against Guanggu and gave the effort everything he had.

sentences.zh: 盧循逼京都，以為督江州、豫州之西陽、新蔡、汝南、潁川、司州之弘農、揚州之松滋六郡諸軍事、建威將軍、江州刺史，從東道出鄱陽。

translations.literal: When Lu Xun pressed upon the capital, Yue was made Supervisor of Military Affairs for Jiang Province and for Xiyang, Xincai, Runan, and Yingchuan in Yu Province, Hongnong in Si Province, and Songzi in Yang Province across six commanderies, General Who Establishes Might, and Inspector of Jiang Province, and advanced by the eastern route through Poyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Lu Xun threatened the capital, Yue was appointed to oversee military affairs in Jiang Province and six commanderies—Xiyang, Xincai, Runan, and Yingchuan in Yu, Hongnong in Si, and Songzi in Yang—and made General Who Establishes Might and Inspector of Jiang Province, marching east through Poyang.

sentences.zh: 循遣將英糾千餘人斷五畝嶠，悅破之，進據豫章，絕循糧援。

translations.literal: Xun sent his general Ying Jiu with more than a thousand men to block Wumu Pass; Yue defeated them, advanced to hold Yuzhang, and cut off Xun's grain and reinforcements.
translations.idiomatic: Xun sent General Ying Jiu with over a thousand men to hold Wumu Pass; Yue routed them, seized Yuzhang, and severed Xun's supply lines.

sentences.zh: 初，毅家在京口，貧約過常，嘗與鄉曲士大夫往東堂共射。

translations.literal: Earlier, Yi's family was at Jingkou, poorer than ordinary, and he had once gone with local gentry to the Eastern Hall to shoot together.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Yi's household was at Jingkou and living more meagerly than most, he had sometimes gone with local gentlemen to shoot at the Eastern Hall.

sentences.zh: 時悅為司徒右長史，暫至京，要府州僚佐共出東堂。

translations.literal: At that time Yue was Right Chief Clerk to the Minister of Works and had come briefly to the capital; he invited colleagues from the prefectural and provincial offices to go out together to the Eastern Hall.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Yue was right chief clerk to the Minister of Works and was briefly in the capital; he invited colleagues from the prefectural and provincial staffs to join him at the Eastern Hall.

sentences.zh: 毅已先至，遣與悅相聞，曰：「身久躓頓，營一遊集甚難。

translations.literal: Yi had already arrived first and sent word to Yue, saying: "I have long been stuck in hardship, and it is very hard to arrange a single outing.
translations.idiomatic: Yi had arrived first and sent word to Yue: "I have been mired in hardship for so long that it is no small thing to arrange even one outing.

sentences.zh: 君如意人，無處不可為適，豈能以此堂見讓。

translations.literal: You are a man who gets his way; there is nowhere you cannot make yourself comfortable—how could you yield this hall to me?"
translations.idiomatic: You are a man who always has his way; you can make yourself comfortable anywhere—surely you would not yield this hall to me?"

sentences.zh: 」悅素豪，徑前，不答毅語。

translations.literal: " Yue was by nature overbearing; he went straight forward and did not answer Yi.
translations.idiomatic: " Yue, who was naturally imperious, walked straight in without answering Yi.

sentences.zh: 眾人並避之，唯毅留射如故。

translations.literal: Everyone else withdrew, but only Yi remained shooting as before.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone else drew aside; only Yi went on shooting as before.

sentences.zh: 悅廚饌甚盛，不以及毅。

translations.literal: Yue's kitchen fare was very lavish, but none of it was extended to Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Yue's table was lavish, yet nothing was sent to Yi.

sentences.zh: 毅既不去，悅甚不歡，俄頃亦退。

translations.literal: Since Yi would not leave, Yue was very displeased and soon withdrew as well.
translations.idiomatic: When Yi still would not leave, Yue grew thoroughly displeased and withdrew himself a little later.

sentences.zh: 毅又相聞曰：「身今年未得子鵝，豈能以殘炙見惠。

translations.literal: Yi sent word again, saying: "This year I have not even gotten a young goose—how could I accept your leftover roast as a favor?"
translations.idiomatic: Yi sent another message: "I have not even had a young goose this year—why should I accept your leftovers as a kindness?"

sentences.zh: 」悅又不答。

translations.literal: " Yue again made no reply.
translations.idiomatic: " Again Yue did not answer.

sentences.zh: 盧循平後，毅求都督江州，以江州內地，治民為職，不宜置軍府，上表陳之曰：「臣聞天以盈虛為道，治以損益為義。

translations.literal: After Lu Xun was pacified, Yi requested supervision of Jiang Province, arguing that Jiang was an interior region whose duty was to govern the people and that a military headquarters should not be placed there; he submitted a memorial stating: "Your servant has heard that Heaven takes fullness and emptiness as its way, and government takes reduction and increase as its principle.
translations.idiomatic: After Lu Xun was defeated, Liu Yi sought to be made military overseer of Jiang Province. He argued that Jiang lay in the interior and that its proper task was civil administration, not the maintenance of a military headquarters, and submitted a memorial: "I have heard that Heaven itself works through waxing and waning, and that sound government works through cutting back and building up.

sentences.zh: 時否而政不革，民凋而事不損，則無以救急病於已危，拯塗炭於將絕。

translations.literal: When the times are adverse yet policy is not reformed, when the people are wasted yet burdens are not reduced, then there is no way to cure an acute illness already critical or to rescue those in the fire and water of imminent ruin.
translations.idiomatic: When times are adverse yet policy stays unchanged, when the people are ruined yet burdens are not lifted, there is no saving a crisis already acute or a people already at the edge of ruin.

sentences.zh: 自頃戎車屢駕，干戈溢境，江州以一隅之地，當逆順之衝，力弱民慢，而器運所繼。

translations.literal: Recently war-chariots have been driven out again and again, and arms have overflowed the borders; Jiang Province, a single corner of the realm, stands at the clash of loyalists and rebels, its strength weak and its people slack, yet the vessels of fortune have passed through it.
translations.idiomatic: Lately campaigns have followed one after another and arms have flooded the borders. Jiang Province is only one corner of the realm, yet it has lain in the path of every clash between rebel and loyalist; weak in force and slack in its people, it has nonetheless borne the full weight of these upheavals.

sentences.zh: 自桓玄以來，驅蹙殘毀，至乃男不被養，女無對匹，逃亡去就，不避幽深，自非財單力竭，無以至此。

translations.literal: Since Huan Xuan's time it has been driven, squeezed, ruined, and destroyed, until men could not be reared and women had no matches; flight and return paid no heed to remoteness—only when wealth was exhausted and strength spent could things reach this point.
translations.idiomatic: Since Huan Xuan's day the region has been harried and laid waste until men could not be raised and women found no husbands; people fled or returned without regard to how deep into the hills they went. Only when households were stripped bare and strength spent could ruin go so far.

sentences.zh: 若不曲心矜理，有所改移，則靡遺之歎，奄焉必及。

translations.literal: If one does not bend the heart to compassionate governance and make some change, then the lament that none remain will come upon us in no time.
translations.idiomatic: Unless the court bends its heart to merciful rule and makes real changes, the lament that none are left will come upon us before long.

sentences.zh: 臣謬荷增統，傷慨兼懷。

translations.literal: Your servant has wrongly received added command and bears grief and indignation together.
translations.idiomatic: I have undeservedly been given added authority, and grief and indignation weigh on me together.

sentences.zh: 夫設官分職，軍國殊用，牧民以息務為大，武略以濟事為先。

translations.literal: In setting offices and dividing duties, army and state have different uses: governing the people takes easing their labors as paramount, while military strategy takes accomplishing the task as foremost.
translations.idiomatic: Offices exist for different purposes in civil and military affairs: governing the people means above all easing their burdens, while military strategy means above all accomplishing the mission.

sentences.zh: 今兼而領之，蓋出於權事，因藉既久，遂為常則。

translations.literal: Today to hold both together came at first from expedient circumstance; because the arrangement has lasted so long, it has become the regular rule.
translations.idiomatic: Combining both roles was at first only an expedient; because the arrangement has lasted so long, it has hardened into custom.

sentences.zh: 江州在腹心之中，憑接揚、豫，藩屏所倚，實為重複。

translations.literal: Jiang Province lies in the heartland, leaning on Yang and Yu as the screen on which the realm relies—it is in truth a duplication.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Province lies in the heartland, adjoining Yang and Yu—the very screen on which the realm relies—so that the present arrangement is truly redundant.

sentences.zh: 昔胡寇縱逸，朔馬臨江，抗禦之宜，蓋出權計。

translations.literal: In the past when barbarian raiders ran wild and northern horses came to the river, the measures for resistance came from expedient planning.
translations.idiomatic: When barbarian raiders once ran wild and northern horses reached the Yangzi, the measures taken for defense were only expedients of the moment.

sentences.zh: 以溫嶠明達，事由一己，猶覺其弊，論之備悉。

translations.literal: Even with Wen Jiao's clarity and penetration, when the matter rested on one man he still felt its harm, and his discussion of it was thorough in every respect.
translations.idiomatic: Even Wen Jiao, clear-sighted as he was, saw the harm when one man held both roles, and discussed the problem at length.

sentences.zh: 今江右區區，戶不盈數十萬，地不逾數千里，而統司鱗次，未獲減息，大而言之，足為國恥。

translations.literal: Today the Jiangyou region is tiny: households do not reach several hundred thousand, and territory does not exceed several thousand li, yet supervisory offices crowd in ranks without relief—speaking broadly, this is enough to be a national disgrace.
translations.idiomatic: Today the lands south of the Yangzi are a narrow strip: fewer than a few hundred thousand households, territory no more than a few thousand li, yet supervisory offices crowd in rank upon rank without relief. Broadly speaking, this is a national disgrace.

sentences.zh: 況乃地在無軍，而軍府猶置，文武將佐，資費非一，豈所謂經國大情，揚湯去火者哉？

translations.literal: Moreover the territory is now without armies, yet the military headquarters still stands, with civil and military aides and assistants whose costs are not few—is this what is called the great principle of ordering the state, skimming the broth to remove the fire?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the region no longer needs an army, yet the military headquarters remains, with all its civil and military staff and their many expenses. Is this the great principle of governing a state—skimming the broth while the fire still burns beneath?

sentences.zh: 其州郡邊江，民戶遼落，加以郵亭嶮闊，畏阻風波，轉輸往還，常有淹廢；

translations.literal: Its prefectures and commanderies border the river; households are sparse and far apart, and in addition the postal stations are perilous and wide apart, so that men fear the blocking of wind and waves and transport back and forth is often delayed and wasted;
translations.idiomatic: Its prefectures and counties line the river; households are sparse and scattered, and the postal stations lie far apart across dangerous waters, so that men fear wind and wave and transport is constantly delayed or lost;

sentences.zh: 又非所謂因其所利，以濟其弊者也。

translations.literal: nor is this what is called using what is advantageous to remedy what is harmed.
translations.idiomatic: nor is this using advantage to remedy harm.

sentences.zh: 愚謂宜解軍府，移治豫章，處十郡之中，厲簡惠之政，比及數年，可有生氣。

translations.literal: This fool thinks the military headquarters should be dissolved, administration moved to Yuzhang, placed among ten commanderies, and a policy of simplicity and kindness enforced—within a few years there could again be vitality.
translations.idiomatic: I believe the military headquarters should be abolished and the seat moved to Yuzhang, placed among ten commanderies, with a policy of simplicity and kindness enforced; within a few years the region could breathe again.

sentences.zh: 且屬縣凋散，亦有所存，而役調送迎，不得休止，亦謂應隨宜並減，以簡眾費。

translations.literal: Moreover the subordinate counties are withered and scattered, yet something of authority still remains, while corvée, transport, and escort duties never cease—I also say they should be reduced as fits the case to ease the multitude of costs.
translations.idiomatic: The outlying counties are ruined, yet escorts and levies never stop; jurisdictions should be merged where possible to cut the waste.

sentences.zh: 刺史庾悅，自臨州部，甚有恤民之誠，但綱維不革，自非綱目所理。

translations.literal: Inspector Yu Yue, since taking charge of the province, has shown great sincerity in pitying the people, but because the net of control is not reformed, what lies outside the main lines cannot be managed.
translations.idiomatic: Inspector Yu Yue has meant well for the people since he arrived, but without structural reform even his zeal cannot reach every problem.

sentences.zh: 尋陽接蠻，宜有防遏，可即州府千兵，以助郡戍。

translations.literal: Xunyang borders the Man tribes and ought to have checks and defenses; a thousand soldiers from the prefectural headquarters may be sent at once to aid the county garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: Xunyang fronts tribal country and needs a visible guard: detach a thousand men from the prefectural army to stiffen the county posts.

sentences.zh: 」於是解悅都督、將軍官，以刺史移鎮豫章。

translations.literal: " Thereupon Yue was relieved of his posts as supervisor and general; as inspector he was moved to garrison Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: " Yue was therefore stripped of his supervisory and general titles and, retaining only his inspectorship, was moved to garrison Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 毅以親將趙恢領千兵守尋陽，建威府文武三千悉入毅府，符攝嚴峻，數相挫辱。

translations.literal: Yi had his trusted general Zhao Hui lead a thousand men to hold Xunyang; all three thousand civil and military staff of the Establishing Might headquarters entered Yi's headquarters, and his orders and summons were severe, repeatedly humiliating Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Yi sent his confidant Zhao Hui with a thousand men to garrison Xunyang, absorbed all three thousand civil and military staff of Yue's former headquarters into his own command, and issued harsh orders that repeatedly humiliated him.

sentences.zh: 悅不得志，疽發背，到豫章少日卒，進年三十八。

translations.literal: Yue did not achieve his aims; a carbuncle broke out on his back, and within a few days after reaching Yuzhang he died, having just entered his thirty-eighth year.
translations.idiomatic: Frustrated in his aims, Yue developed a carbuncle on his back and died within a few days of reaching Yuzhang, aged thirty-eight.

sentences.zh: 追贈征虜將軍。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was given the title General Who Campaigns Against Barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made General Who Campaigns Against Barbarians.

sentences.zh: 以廣固之功，追封新陽縣五等男。

translations.literal: For his achievement at Guanggu he was posthumously enfeoffed as Baron of the Fifth Rank of Xinyang County.
translations.idiomatic: For his service at Guanggu he was posthumously enfeoffed as fifth-rank baron of Xinyang County.

sentences.zh: 王誕，字茂世，琅邪臨沂人，太保弘從兄也。

translations.literal: Wang Dan, courtesy name Maoshi, was a native of Linyi in Langye, a cousin of the Grand Guardian Hong on the father's side.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dan, styled Maoshi, came from Linyi in Langye Commandery and was a paternal cousin of Grand Guardian Wang Hong.

sentences.zh: 祖恬，中軍將軍。

translations.literal: His grandfather Tian was General of the Center Army.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Tian had been General of the Center Army.

sentences.zh: 父混，太常。

translations.literal: His father Hun was Grand Master of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: His father Hun had served as Grand Master of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 誕少有才藻，晉孝武帝崩，從叔尚書令珣為哀策文，久而未就，謂誕曰：「猶少序節物一句。

translations.literal: Dan in his youth had literary talent. When Emperor Xiaowu of Jin died, his uncle by the father's side, Minister of Works Xun, was drafting the lamentation text but for a long time had not finished; he said to Dan: "I still lack a line ordering the seasonal things.
translations.idiomatic: Dan showed literary talent early. When Emperor Xiaowu of Jin died, his father's cousin Xun, then Minister of Works, was drafting the lamentation but could not finish it; he told Dan, "I still lack a line on the seasonal turn.

sentences.zh: 」因出本示誕。

translations.literal: " He thereupon brought out the draft to show Dan.
translations.idiomatic: " He showed Dan the draft.

sentences.zh: 誕攬筆便益之，接其「秋冬代變」後云：「霜繁廣除，風回高殿。

translations.literal: Dan took up the brush and at once added to it, following after "autumn and winter succeed one another" with the words: "Frost thick on the broad courts, wind circling the lofty halls.
translations.idiomatic: Dan took the brush and at once added a line after "autumn and winter give way to one another": "Frost thickens in the broad courts; wind circles the lofty halls.

sentences.zh: 」珣嗟歎清拔，因而用之。

translations.literal: " Xun sighed in admiration at its clarity and elevation and used it accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: " Xun marveled at its clarity and kept the line.

sentences.zh: 襲爵雉鄉侯，拜秘書郎，琅邪王文學，中軍功曹。

translations.literal: He inherited the title Marquis of Zhixiang, was appointed Gentleman of the Secretariat, Literary Scholar to the Prince of Langye, and Merit Officer of the Center Army.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited the marquisate of Zhixiang, became gentleman of the Secretariat, literary scholar to the Prince of Langye, and merit officer of the center army.

sentences.zh: 隆安四年，會稽王世子元顯開後軍府，又以誕補功曹。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Long'an, the Heir of the Prince of Kuaiji, Yuanxian, opened a Rear Army headquarters, and Dan was again appointed Merit Officer.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Long'an, when Kuaiji heir Yuanxian opened a rear army headquarters, Dan was again made merit officer.

sentences.zh: 尋除尚書吏部郎，仍為後軍長史，領廬江太守，加鎮蠻護軍。

translations.literal: Soon he was made Gentleman of the Ministry of Personnel in the Secretariat, and still served as Chief Clerk of the Rear Army, holding concurrently the post of Administrator of Lujiang and added Protector of the Army Who Pacifies the Barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made gentleman of the Ministry of Personnel, while continuing as chief clerk of the rear army, concurrently administering Lujiang and serving as protector of the army who pacifies the barbarians.

sentences.zh: 轉龍驤將軍、琅邪內史，長史如故。

translations.literal: He was transferred to General of the Dragon Cavalry and Interior Minister of Langye, his chief clerkship remaining as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to General of the Dragon Cavalry and Interior Minister of Langye, retaining his post as chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 誕結事元顯嬖人張法順，故為元顯所寵。

translations.literal: Dan cultivated ties with Yuanxian's favorite Zhang Fashun and therefore was cherished by Yuanxian.
translations.idiomatic: Dan cultivated Zhang Fashun, Yuanxian's favorite, and thereby won Yuanxian's favor.

sentences.zh: 元顯納妾，誕為之親迎。

translations.literal: When Yuanxian took a concubine, Dan went in person to welcome her for him.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuanxian took a concubine, Dan went in person to fetch her for him.

sentences.zh: 隨府轉驃騎長史，將軍、內史如故。

translations.literal: When the headquarters was transferred he became Chief Clerk of the Rapid Cavalry, his generalship and interior ministership remaining as before.
translations.idiomatic: When the headquarters shifted he became chief clerk of the Rapid Cavalry, keeping his general's rank and interior ministership.

sentences.zh: 元顯討桓玄，欲悉誅桓氏，誕固陳脩等與玄志趣不同，由此得免。

translations.literal: When Yuanxian campaigned against Huan Xuan he wished to execute the whole Huan clan; Dan firmly stated that Xiu and others did not share Xuan's aims, and by this they were spared.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuanxian marched against Huan Xuan he meant to execute the entire Huan clan; Dan argued firmly that Xiu and others did not share Xuan's aims, and they were spared.

sentences.zh: 脩，誕甥也。

translations.literal: Xiu was Dan's nephew by a sister.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu was Dan's nephew.

sentences.zh: 及玄得志，誕將見誅，脩為之陳請；

translations.literal: When Xuan gained power, Dan was about to be executed, and Xiu pleaded on his behalf;
translations.idiomatic: When Xuan seized power, Dan was to be executed; Xiu pleaded for him;

sentences.zh: 又言脩等得免之由，乃徙誕廣州。

translations.literal: he also explained the reason Xiu and the others had been spared, and Dan was then banished to Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: and, citing the reason Xiu and the others had been spared, had Dan banished to Guangzhou instead.

sentences.zh: 盧循據廣州。

translations.literal: Lu Xun held Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Xun seized Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 以誕為其平南府長史，甚賓禮之。

translations.literal: He made Dan Chief Clerk of his Pacify-the-South headquarters and treated him with great courtesy as a guest.
translations.idiomatic: He made Dan chief clerk of his Pacify-the-South headquarters and honored him as a distinguished guest.

sentences.zh: 誕久客思歸，乃說循曰：「下官流遠在此，被蒙殊眷，士感知己，實思報答。

translations.literal: Dan, long a guest and longing to return, then urged Xun, saying: "Your humble servant has been cast far off here and has received extraordinary favor; a gentleman who knows a benefactor truly wishes to repay him.
translations.idiomatic: Longing to go home after years as a guest, Dan urged Xun: "I have been cast far from home yet have received extraordinary favor from you; a gentleman who knows his benefactor longs to repay him.

sentences.zh: 本非戎旅，在此無用。

translations.literal: I am by nature no man of the army and am of no use here.
translations.idiomatic: I am no soldier and am of no use here.

sentences.zh: 素為劉鎮軍所識，情味不淺，若得北歸，必蒙任寄，公私際會，思報厚恩，愈於停此，空移歲月。

translations.literal: I have long been known to General Liu the Pacifier, and our bond is not shallow; if I could return north I would surely be entrusted with office; at the juncture of public and private affairs I would think to repay your deep kindness—better than staying here and letting the months pass in vain.
translations.idiomatic: Liu the Pacifier has known me for years and thinks well of me; if I return north he will surely employ me, and at the right moment I could repay your kindness far better than by sitting here while the months slip away.

sentences.zh: 」循甚然之。

translations.literal: " Xun greatly approved.
translations.idiomatic: " Xun agreed wholeheartedly.

sentences.zh: 時廣州刺史吳隱之亦為循所拘留，誕又曰：「將軍今留吳公，公私非計。

translations.literal: At that time the Inspector of Guangzhou, Wu Yin, was also detained by Xun; Dan added: "General, to keep Lord Wu now is no plan for public or private good.
translations.idiomatic: Inspector Wu Yin of Guangzhou was also being held; Dan added, "General, keeping Lord Wu is poor policy for you both.

sentences.zh: 孫伯符豈不欲留華子魚，但以一境不容二君耳。

translations.literal: Did Sun Bofu not wish to keep Hua Ziyu? Yet one territory cannot hold two lords.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ce wanted to keep Hua Ziyu too, but one province cannot hold two masters.

sentences.zh: 」於是誕及隱之並得還。

translations.literal: " Thereupon both Dan and Yin were able to return.
translations.idiomatic: " Both Dan and Yin were allowed to return.

sentences.zh: 除員外散騎常侍，未拜，高祖請為太尉諮議參軍，轉長史。

translations.literal: He was appointed Extraordinary Attendant Cavalier-in-Ordinary but had not yet received the investiture when the High Ancestor invited him to be Advising Retainer to the Grand Commandant, then transferred him to Chief Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed extraordinary attendant cavalier-in-ordinary but had not yet taken up the post when the High Ancestor made him advising retainer to the Grand Commandant, then chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 盡心歸奉，日夜不懈，高祖甚委仗之。

translations.literal: He devoted his heart to service without slackening day or night, and the High Ancestor greatly relied on him.
translations.idiomatic: He served with tireless devotion day and night, and the High Ancestor came to rely on him heavily.

sentences.zh: 北伐廣固，領齊郡太守。

translations.literal: On the northern campaign against Guanggu he held concurrently the post of Administrator of Qi Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: On the northern campaign against Guanggu he concurrently administered Qi Commandery.

sentences.zh: 盧循自蔡洲南走，劉毅固求追討，高祖持疑未決，誕密白曰：「公既平廣固，復滅盧循，則功蓋終古，勳無與二，如此大威，豈可餘人分之。

translations.literal: When Lu Xun fled south from Caizhou, Liu Yi firmly asked to pursue and attack; the High Ancestor hesitated and had not decided when Dan secretly reported: "Your Lordship has already pacified Guanggu; if you also destroy Lu Xun, your achievement will cover all antiquity and your merit will have no second—such great authority, how could it be shared with others?"
translations.idiomatic: When Lu Xun fled south from Caizhou, Liu Yi pressed hard for permission to pursue; the High Ancestor hesitated, and Dan privately urged him: "You have already taken Guanggu; if you also destroy Lu Xun, your achievement will surpass all antiquity and your merit will stand alone. Such authority cannot be shared."

sentences.zh: 毅與公同起布衣，一時相推耳。

translations.literal: Yi rose with Your Lordship from common cloth and was for a time pushed forward together—that is all.
translations.idiomatic: Yi rose with you from common cloth and was your peer for a time—that is all.

sentences.zh: 今既已喪敗，不宜復使立功。

translations.literal: Now that he has already been defeated, he should not be allowed to win merit again.
translations.idiomatic: Now that he has been defeated, he should not be allowed to win glory again.

sentences.zh: 」高祖從其說。

translations.literal: " The High Ancestor followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: " The High Ancestor took his advice.

sentences.zh: 七年，以誕為吳國內史。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he made Dan Interior Minister of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he made Dan interior minister of Wu.

sentences.zh: 母憂去職。

translations.literal: He left office on his mother's mourning.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned to observe mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 高祖征劉毅，起為輔國將軍，誕固辭軍號，墨絰從行。

translations.literal: When the High Ancestor campaigned against Liu Yi he was recalled as General Who Assists the State; Dan firmly declined the military title and followed in unbleached hemp mourning dress.
translations.idiomatic: When the High Ancestor marched against Liu Yi, Dan was recalled as general who assists the state but firmly declined the military title and followed in unbleached mourning dress.

sentences.zh: 時諸葛長民行太尉留府事，心不自安，高祖甚慮之。

translations.literal: At that time Zhuge Changmin was acting Grand Commandant and remaining to handle headquarters affairs; he was ill at ease in his heart, and the High Ancestor was very concerned about him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Changmin was then acting as Grand Commandant in the capital and was ill at ease; the High Ancestor was deeply worried about him.

sentences.zh: 毅既平，誕求先下，高祖曰：「長民似有自疑心，卿詎宜便去。

translations.literal: After Yi was pacified, Dan asked to go down ahead; the High Ancestor said: "Changmin seems to harbor doubts about himself—how could you suitably leave at once?"
translations.idiomatic: After Yi was defeated, Dan asked to return to the capital ahead of the army; the High Ancestor said, "Changmin seems uneasy in his mind—surely you should not leave yet."

sentences.zh: 」誕曰：「長民知我蒙公垂眄，今輕身單下，必當以為無虞，乃可以少安其意。

translations.literal: " Dan said: "Changmin knows that I have received Your Lordship's gracious regard; if I now go down lightly and alone, he will surely take it that there is nothing to fear, and thus his mind can be somewhat eased.
translations.idiomatic: " Dan replied, "Changmin knows I enjoy your favor; if I return alone and unarmed, he will think there is nothing to fear and his mind will be eased.

sentences.zh: 」高祖笑曰：「卿勇過賁、育矣。

translations.literal: " The High Ancestor laughed and said: "Your courage surpasses Ben and Yu.
translations.idiomatic: " The High Ancestor laughed and said, "Your courage surpasses the heroes Ben and Yu.

sentences.zh: 」於是先還。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he returned first.
translations.idiomatic: " He was therefore allowed to return first.

sentences.zh: 九年，卒，時年三十九。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he died, aged thirty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he died, aged thirty-nine.

sentences.zh: 以南北從征，追封作唐縣五等侯。

translations.literal: For following the campaigns north and south he was posthumously enfeoffed as Marquis of the Fifth Rank of Zuotang County.
translations.idiomatic: For his service on the northern and southern campaigns he was posthumously enfeoffed as fifth-rank marquis of Zuotang County.

sentences.zh: 子詡，宋世子舍人，早卒。

translations.literal: His son Xu was Attendant to the Heir of Song and died young.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xu served as attendant to the heir of Song and died young.

sentences.zh: 謝景仁

translations.literal: Xie Jingren
translations.idiomatic: Xie Jingren

sentences.zh: 謝景仁，陳郡陽夏人，衛將軍晦從叔父也。

translations.literal: Xie Jingren was a native of Yangxia in Chen Commandery, a father's younger cousin of General of the Guard Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Jingren came from Yangxia in Chen Commandery and was a paternal cousin of General of the Guard Xie Hui.

sentences.zh: 名與高祖同諱，故稱字。

translations.literal: His personal name shared a taboo with the High Ancestor, so he is called by his courtesy name.
translations.idiomatic: His personal name tabooed that of the High Ancestor, so the text uses his courtesy name.

sentences.zh: 祖據，太傅安第二弟。

translations.literal: His grandfather Ju was the Grand Tutor An's second younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Ju was the second younger brother of Grand Tutor Xie An.

sentences.zh: 父允，宣城內史。

translations.literal: His father Yun was Interior Minister of Xuancheng.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yun had been interior minister of Xuancheng.

sentences.zh: 景仁幼時與安相及，為安所知。

translations.literal: In his youth Jingren was of an age with An and was recognized by An.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy Jingren was close in age to Xie An and won his notice.

sentences.zh: 始為前軍行參軍、輔國參軍事。

translations.literal: At first he served as Acting Retainer of the Forward Army and Staff Officer of the Army Who Supports the State.
translations.idiomatic: He first served as acting retainer of the Forward Army and staff officer of the Army Who Supports the State.

sentences.zh: 會稽王世子元顯嬖人張法順，權傾一時，內外無不造門者，唯景仁不至。

translations.literal: The favorite of Kuaiji Heir Yuanxian, Zhang Fashun, had power that tilted the age; inside and outside none failed to visit his gate—only Jingren did not come.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Fashun, favorite of Kuaiji heir Yuan Xian, wielded power that dominated the court; everyone high and low came to his door—everyone but Jingren.

sentences.zh: 年三十，方為著作佐郎。

translations.literal: At age thirty he was only then made Assistant Gentleman of the Directorate of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He was thirty before he was finally made assistant gentleman of the Directorate of Writing.

sentences.zh: 桓玄誅元顯，見景仁，甚知之，謂四坐曰：「司馬庶人父子云何不敗，遂令謝景仁三十方作著作佐郎。

translations.literal: Huan Xuan executed Yuanxian; when he saw Jingren he greatly recognized his quality and said to those seated: "How is it that the Sima commoners, father and son, did not fall to ruin—yet they let Xie Jingren become Assistant Gentleman of the Directorate of Writing only at thirty?
translations.idiomatic: After Huan Xuan killed Yuan Xian, he met Jingren and was much impressed; addressing the assembly he said, "How did the Sima upstarts, father and son, fail to ruin the realm—only to leave Xie Jingren no better than assistant gentleman of the Directorate of Writing at thirty?

sentences.zh: 」玄為太尉，以補行參軍，府轉大將軍，仍參軍事。

translations.literal: " When Xuan became Grand Commandant he appointed Jingren Acting Retainer; when the headquarters was transferred to Great General he still served on staff.
translations.idiomatic: " After Xuan became Grand Commandant he made Jingren acting retainer; when the office became a great general's headquarters Jingren remained on staff.

sentences.zh: 玄建楚臺，以補黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: When Xuan established the Chu Tower he appointed Jingren Gentleman Attendant at the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuan established the Chu Tower he made Jingren Gentleman Attendant at the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 及篡位，領驍騎將軍。

translations.literal: When he usurped the throne, Jingren held the post of General of Valiant Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: After the usurpation Jingren served as General of Valiant Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 景仁博聞強識，善敘前言往行，玄每與之言，不倦也。

translations.literal: Jingren was broadly learned and strongly retentive in memory, skilled at recounting former words and past conduct; Xuan whenever spoke with him was never weary of it.
translations.idiomatic: Jingren was widely learned with a formidable memory and a gift for recounting earlier sayings and past deeds; Xuan could talk with him endlessly without tiring.

sentences.zh: 玄出行，殷仲文、卞範之之徒，皆騎馬散從，而使景仁陪輦。

translations.literal: When Xuan went out, Yin Zhongwen, Bian Fanzhi, and men of that sort all rode horses scattered in attendance, but had Jingren accompany the carriage.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuan went abroad, Yin Zhongwen, Bian Fanzhi, and their circle rode as a loose mounted escort while Jingren alone rode beside the imperial carriage.

sentences.zh: 高祖為桓脩撫軍中兵參軍，嘗詣景仁諮事，景仁與語悅之，因留高祖共食。

translations.literal: The High Ancestor was Major of the Center Army under Huan Xiu's Pacifying Army; he once went to Jingren to consult on business; Jingren was pleased in speaking with him and therefore kept the High Ancestor to eat together.
translations.idiomatic: When the High Ancestor was major of the center army under Huan Xiu's Pacifying Army, he once visited Jingren on business; Jingren enjoyed their talk and kept him to share a meal.

sentences.zh: 食未辦，而景仁為玄所召。

translations.literal: The food was not yet prepared when Jingren was summoned by Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Before the meal was ready Jingren was summoned by Xuan.

sentences.zh: 玄性促急，俄頃之間，騎詔續至。

translations.literal: Xuan's nature was urgent and hasty; within a moment mounted summonses arrived in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan was impatient by nature; within moments mounted messengers arrived one after another with summons.

sentences.zh: 高祖屢求去，景仁不許，曰：「主上見待，要應有方。

translations.literal: The High Ancestor repeatedly asked to leave; Jingren would not allow it and said: "When the sovereign receives one, there must be a proper way.
translations.idiomatic: The High Ancestor asked repeatedly to go; Jingren refused and said, "When one's lord receives a guest, there ought to be a proper way to do it.

sentences.zh: 我欲與客共食，豈當不得待。

translations.literal: I wish to eat together with my guest—how could I not wait?
translations.idiomatic: I mean to dine with my guest—surely I can wait.

sentences.zh: 」竟安坐飽食，然後應召。

translations.literal: " In the end he sat at ease, ate his fill, and only then answered the summons.
translations.idiomatic: " He sat calmly, ate his fill, and only then answered the summons.

sentences.zh: 高祖甚感之，常謂景仁是太傅安孫。

translations.literal: The High Ancestor was deeply moved by this and often said Jingren was Grand Tutor An's grandson.
translations.idiomatic: The High Ancestor was deeply touched and often remarked that Jingren was the grandson of Grand Tutor Xie An.

sentences.zh: 及平京邑，入鎮石頭，景仁與百僚同見高祖，高祖目之曰：「此名公孫也。

translations.literal: When the capital region was pacified and he entered to garrison Stone City, Jingren went with the hundred officials to see the High Ancestor; the High Ancestor fixed his gaze on him and said: "This is the grandson of a famous lord.
translations.idiomatic: After the capital was secured and he entered Stone City, Jingren came with the officials to see the High Ancestor, who looked him over and said, "There is the grandson of a great house.

sentences.zh: 」謂景仁曰：「承制府須記室參軍，今當相屈。

translations.literal: " He said to Jingren: "The headquarters acting on imperial authority needs a Record-Office Retainer; I must now impose on you.
translations.idiomatic: " He told Jingren, "The provisional headquarters needs a record-office retainer—I must ask you to take the post.

sentences.zh: 」以為大將軍武陵王遵記室參軍，仍為從事中郎，遷司徒左長史。

translations.literal: " He was made Record-Office Retainer to Great General the Prince of Wuling Zun, still served as Attendant Gentleman, and was promoted to Left Chief Clerk of the Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: " Jingren was made record-office retainer to Great General Prince Zun of Wuling, continued as attendant gentleman, and was promoted to left chief clerk of the Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 出為高祖鎮軍司馬，領晉陵太守，復為車騎司馬。

translations.literal: He went out as Major of the Pacifying Army to the High Ancestor, holding concurrently the post of Administrator of Jinling, then again served as Major of the Chariots and Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He served as the High Ancestor's Pacifying Army major and concurrently as administrator of Jinling, then again as major of the Chariots and Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 義熙五年，高祖以內難既寧，思弘外略，將伐鮮卑；

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yixi the High Ancestor, since internal trouble was already settled, thought to expand outward strategy and was about to campaign against the Xianbei;
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Yixi, with internal troubles settled, the High Ancestor planned an outward offensive and intended to campaign against the Xianbei;

sentences.zh: 朝議皆謂不可。

translations.literal: Court deliberation all deemed it impossible.
translations.idiomatic: The court unanimously opposed the idea.

sentences.zh: 劉毅時鎮姑孰，固止高祖，以為：「苻堅侵境，謝太傅猶不自行。

translations.literal: Liu Yi at that time garrisoned Gucheng and firmly stopped the High Ancestor, stating: "When Fu Jian invaded the borders, Grand Tutor Xie still did not go in person.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yi, then stationed at Gucheng, firmly opposed the High Ancestor, arguing, "When Fu Jian invaded the realm, Grand Tutor Xie did not take the field himself.

sentences.zh: 宰相遠出，傾動根本。

translations.literal: The chief minister going far away would overturn and shake the foundation.
translations.idiomatic: For the chief minister to march far afield would upset the foundations of power.

sentences.zh: 」景仁獨曰：「公建桓、文之烈，應天人之心，匡復皇祚，芟夷奸逆，雖業高振古，而德刑未孚，宜推亡固存，廣樹威略。

translations.literal: " Jingren alone said: "Your lordship has raised the glory of Duke Huan and Duke Wen, answered the hearts of Heaven and men, restored the imperial throne, and cut down treachery and rebellion; though your achievement towers above antiquity, virtue and punishment have not yet won universal trust—you should pursue the perishing and strengthen the surviving and broadly plant authority and strategy.
translations.idiomatic: " Jingren alone spoke up: "You have raised achievements like those of Duke Huan and Duke Wen, answered Heaven and the people, restored the throne, and uprooted treachery; though your feats surpass antiquity, your moral sway is not yet secure—you should press the doomed and strengthen the loyal and extend your authority far and wide.

sentences.zh: 鮮卑密邇疆甸，屢犯邊垂，伐罪弔民，於是乎在。

translations.literal: The Xianbei are close upon the border lands and repeatedly violate the frontier—punishing crime and comforting the people lies precisely here.
translations.idiomatic: The Xianbei press close upon our borders and raid again and again; here is where we punish the guilty and succor the people.

sentences.zh: 平定之後，養銳息徒，然後觀兵洛汭，修復園寢，豈有坐長寇虜，縱敵貽患者哉！

translations.literal: After pacification, sharpen the keen and rest the troops—then review arms at the Luo Ford and restore the imperial tombs and parks—how could one sit and lengthen the brigand invaders, indulging the enemy and leaving calamity behind!
translations.idiomatic: Once they are subdued, we can rest our troops and then parade forces at the Luo ford and restore the imperial tombs—how can we sit by while the enemy grows strong and leave trouble to fester!

sentences.zh: 」高祖納之。

translations.literal: " The High Ancestor accepted this.
translations.idiomatic: " The High Ancestor accepted his counsel.

sentences.zh: 及北伐，大司馬琅邪王，天子母弟，屬當儲副，高祖深以根本為憂，轉景仁為大司馬左司馬，專總府任，右衛將軍，加給事中，又遷吏部尚書。

translations.literal: On the northern campaign, the Great Minister of State the Prince of Langye, the Son of Heaven's younger brother by the same mother, was by rank heir apparent—the High Ancestor deeply worried over the foundation and transferred Jingren to Left Major of the Great Minister of State, specially supervising headquarters duties, Right Guard General, added Attendant at the Court, and again promoted him to Minister of the Civil Service.
translations.idiomatic: When the northern campaign began, the Heir Apparent's younger brother, Prince of Langye, held the great minister of state post, and the High Ancestor, deeply worried for the capital, made Jingren left major of that office with full authority over headquarters affairs, Right Guard General, and attendant at court, then Minister of the Civil Service.

sentences.zh: 時從兄混為左僕射，依制不得相臨，高祖啟依僕射王彪之、尚書王劭前例，不解職。

translations.literal: At that time his father's elder brother's son Hun was Left Vice Director; by regulation they could not oversee each other; the High Ancestor memorialized following the prior precedents of Vice Director Wang Biaozhi and Minister Wang Shao, not relieving either from office.
translations.idiomatic: His cousin Hun was then left vice director; regulations barred mutual oversight, but the High Ancestor petitioned to follow the precedents of Wang Biaozhi and Wang Shao and leave both in office.

sentences.zh: 坐選吏部令史邢安泰為都令史、平原太守，二官共除，安泰以令史職拜謁陵廟，為御史中丞鄭鮮之所糾，白衣領職。

translations.literal: He was impeached for appointing Ministry of Personnel clerk Xing Antai as Chief Clerk and Administrator of Pingyuan, the two offices concurrently dismissed—Antai in his capacity as clerk attended the imperial tombs and shrines, and was charged by Imperial Secretary Zheng Xianzhi; Jingren wore white and continued in office.
translations.idiomatic: He was censured for appointing Ministry of Personnel clerk Xing Antai concurrently as chief clerk and administrator of Pingyuan; Antai, acting in his clerk's capacity, performed rites at the imperial tombs, and Censor-in-Chief Zheng Xianzhi impeached him—Jingren was stripped of court dress but kept his post.

sentences.zh: 八年，遷領軍將軍。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was transferred to General of the Palace Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he became General of the Palace Guard.

sentences.zh: 十一年，轉右僕射，仍轉左僕射。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was transferred to Right Vice Director, then again to Left Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he was made right vice director, then left vice director.

sentences.zh: 景仁性矜嚴整潔，居宇靜麗，每唾，轉唾左右人衣；

translations.literal: Jingren's nature was austere, stern, and neat; his dwelling was quiet and elegant; whenever he spat, he turned and spat on the clothes of those beside him;
translations.idiomatic: Jingren was fastidious, austere, and immaculate; his rooms were quiet and elegant, and whenever he needed to spit he would turn and expect an attendant's sleeve to receive it;

sentences.zh: 事畢，即聽一日浣濯。

translations.literal: When the matter was finished, he at once allowed one day's washing.
translations.idiomatic: After which the attendant was given a day off to wash the garment.

sentences.zh: 每欲唾，左右爭來受。

translations.literal: Whenever he wished to spit, those beside him competed to come receive it.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he was about to spit, attendants vied to catch it.

sentences.zh: 高祖雅相重，申以婚姻，廬陵王義真妃，景仁女也。

translations.literal: The High Ancestor greatly esteemed him in his own manner and joined them by marriage—the consort of the Prince of Luling Yizhen was Jingren's daughter.
translations.idiomatic: The High Ancestor held him in high regard and bound their houses by marriage: Prince Yizhen of Luling's consort was Jingren's daughter.

sentences.zh: 十二年，卒，時年四十七。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he died, aged forty-seven at the time.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he died, aged forty-seven.

sentences.zh: 追贈金紫光祿大夫，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Master of the Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon, added Regular Attendant at the Palace Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Grand Master of the Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon with the added title Regular Attendant at the Palace Writing.

sentences.zh: 葬日，高祖親臨，哭之甚慟。

translations.literal: On the day of burial the High Ancestor came in person and wept for him with extreme grief.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of the funeral the High Ancestor came in person and wept with deep grief.

sentences.zh: 與驃騎將軍道憐書曰：「謝景仁殞逝，悲痛摧割，不能自勝。

translations.literal: He wrote to Rapid Cavalry General Daolian, saying: "Xie Jingren has died; grief and anguish cut me—I cannot overcome it myself.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote to Rapid Cavalry General Daolian: "Xie Jingren is dead; grief cuts me to the quick and I cannot bear it.

sentences.zh: 汝聞問惋愕，亦不可堪。

translations.literal: When you hear and inquire you will be startled in regret and also unable to bear it.
translations.idiomatic: When you hear of it you will be stricken and overwhelmed as well.

sentences.zh: 其器體淹中，情寄實重，方欲與之共康時務，一旦至此，痛惜兼深。

translations.literal: His capacity and bearing were balanced and centered; the trust placed in him was truly weighty—I was just about to join with him in securing the affairs of the age, and suddenly it came to this—the pain and regret are both deep.
translations.idiomatic: He was balanced in talent and bearing and I relied on him deeply; I had meant to set the age right with him, and now this—my grief and regret are boundless.

sentences.zh: 往矣柰何！

translations.literal: He is gone—what can be done!
translations.idiomatic: He is gone—what can I do!

sentences.zh: 當復柰何！」

translations.literal: What can be done now!"
translations.idiomatic: What is left for me now!"

sentences.zh: 子恂，鄱陽太守。

translations.literal: His son Xun was Administrator of Poyang.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xun was administrator of Poyang.

sentences.zh: 恂子稚，善吹笙。

translations.literal: Xun's son Zhi was skilled at playing the sheng.
translations.idiomatic: Xun's son Zhi was an accomplished sheng player.

sentences.zh: 官至西陽太守。

translations.literal: His office reached Administrator of Xiyang.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to administrator of Xiyang.

sentences.zh: 景仁弟純，字景懋，初為劉毅豫州別駕。

translations.literal: Jingren's younger brother Chun, courtesy name Jingmao, at first served as Administrative Aide of Yu Province under Liu Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Jingren's younger brother Chun, styled Jingmao, first served as Liu Yi's administrative aide for Yu Province.

sentences.zh: 毅鎮江陵，以為衛軍長史、南平相。

translations.literal: When Yi garrisoned Jiangling he made Chun Chief Clerk of the Guard Army and Chancellor of Nanping.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yi held Jiangling he made Chun chief clerk of the Guard Army and chancellor of Nanping.

sentences.zh: 王鎮惡率軍襲毅，已至城下，時毅疾病，佐吏皆入參承。

translations.literal: Wang Zhen'e led troops to strike Yi and had already reached below the city wall; at that time Yi was ill and assistant officials all entered to attend and receive orders.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhen'e led a surprise attack on Liu Yi and reached the city walls; Yi was ill and his staff were all inside attending him.

sentences.zh: 純參承畢，已出，聞兵至，馳還入府。

translations.literal: Chun finished attending and receiving orders and had already gone out; hearing troops had arrived he galloped back and entered the headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Chun had finished his duties and left the hall; hearing that troops had arrived he raced back into headquarters.

sentences.zh: 左右引車欲還外解，純叱之曰：「我人吏也，逃欲何之！

translations.literal: Those beside him pulled the carriage wishing to return to the outer offices; Chun rebuked them, saying: "I am this man's official—where do you think you are fleeing!
translations.idiomatic: His attendants tried to turn the carriage toward the outer offices; Chun shouted, "I am Lord Liu's officer—where do you mean to run!

sentences.zh: 」乃入。

translations.literal: " Then he entered.
translations.idiomatic: " Then he went in.

sentences.zh: 及毅兵敗眾散，時已暗夜，司馬毛脩之謂純曰：「君但隨僕。

translations.literal: When Yi's troops were defeated and the hosts scattered, it was already dark night; Major Mao Xiuzhi said to Chun: "Sir, just follow me.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yi's forces were routed and scattered, night had fallen; Major Mao Xiuzhi told Chun, "Come with me.

sentences.zh: 」純不從，扶兩人出，火光中為人所殺。

translations.literal: " Chun did not follow; supporting the two men he went out and in the firelight was killed by someone.
translations.idiomatic: " Chun refused; supporting the two men he went out and was cut down in the firelight.

sentences.zh: 純孫沈，太宗泰始初，為巴陵王休若衛軍錄事參軍、山陰令，坐事誅。

translations.literal: Chun's grandson Shen, at the beginning of Taishi under Emperor Taizong, served as Recording Retainer of the Guard Army to the Prince of Baling Xiuruo and Magistrate of Shanyin; he was executed on account of an offense.
translations.idiomatic: Chun's grandson Shen, early in Taishi under Emperor Taizong, was recording retainer under Prince Xiuruo of Baling's Guard Army and magistrate of Shanyin; he was executed for an offense.

sentences.zh: 純弟述

translations.literal: Chun's younger brother Shu
translations.idiomatic: Chun's younger brother Shu

sentences.zh: 述字景先，少有志行，隨兄純在江陵。

translations.literal: Shu, courtesy name Jingxian, in youth had aspiration and conduct; he followed his elder brother Chun at Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: Shu, styled Jingxian, showed purpose and integrity from youth and followed his brother Chun at Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 純遇害，述奉純喪還都。

translations.literal: When Chun met with calamity Shu conveyed Chun's coffin back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: After Chun was killed Shu escorted his coffin back to the capital.

sentences.zh: 行至西塞，值暴風，純喪舫流漂，不知所在，述乘小船尋求之。

translations.literal: When the journey reached Xisai they encountered a violent wind; Chun's bier-boat drifted away and its whereabouts were unknown; Shu took a small boat to search for it.
translations.idiomatic: At Xisai a violent storm struck; the boat carrying Chun's coffin broke loose and vanished; Shu took a small boat to search for it.

sentences.zh: 經純妻庾舫過，庾遣人謂述曰：「喪舫存沒，已應有在，風波如此，豈可小船所冒？

translations.literal: Passing the boat of Chun's wife Yu, Yu sent someone to say to Shu: "Whether the bier-boat survives or is lost, its fate should already be settled; with waves and wind like this, how could a small boat dare to venture?
translations.idiomatic: Passing the boat of Chun's widow Yu, she sent word to Shu: "Whether the coffin boat survives or is lost is already fated; in such a storm how can a small boat risk it?

sentences.zh: 小郎去必無及，寧可存亡俱盡邪？

translations.literal: Little brother, if you go you surely will not arrive in time—how could both living and dead be destroyed together?
translations.idiomatic: Young master, you cannot reach it in time—you would not throw your life away with his, would you?

sentences.zh: 」述號泣答曰：「若安全至岸，當須營理。

translations.literal: " Shu wailed and answered: "If it safely reaches shore, I must still arrange matters.
translations.idiomatic: " Shu wept and replied, "If it reaches shore safely I must see to the burial.

sentences.zh: 如其已致意外，述亦無心獨存。

translations.literal: If it has already met mishap, Shu also has no heart to remain alive alone.
translations.idiomatic: If it is already lost I have no wish to live on alone.

sentences.zh: 」因冒浪而進，見純喪幾沒，述號叫呼天，幸而獲免，咸以為精誠所致也。

translations.literal: " Then braving the waves he advanced; he saw Chun's coffin nearly submerged; Shu wailed and called to Heaven; fortunately they escaped harm—all regarded it as brought about by sincere devotion.
translations.idiomatic: " He pushed through the waves, found the coffin nearly sunk, and cried to Heaven; by fortune both were saved, and all took it as the work of his devotion.

sentences.zh: 高祖聞而嘉之，及臨豫州，諷中正以述為主簿，甚被知器。

translations.literal: The High Ancestor heard and commended this; when he came to Yu Province he hinted to the Rectifier of Standards to make Shu Chief Clerk; he was greatly recognized and trusted.
translations.idiomatic: The High Ancestor heard of this and praised him; when he took charge of Yu Province he urged the local standard-grader to appoint Shu chief clerk, and Shu won his trust and esteem.

sentences.zh: 景仁愛其第三弟甝而憎述，嘗設饌請高祖，希命甝豫坐，而高祖召述。

translations.literal: Jingren loved his third younger brother Ping and disliked Shu; he once set out a feast to invite the High Ancestor, hoping to have Ping join the seating, but the High Ancestor summoned Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Jingren favored his third brother Ping and disliked Shu; once when he invited the High Ancestor to dine he hoped Ping would sit with them, but the High Ancestor sent for Shu instead.

sentences.zh: 述知非景仁夙意，又慮高祖命之，請急不從。

translations.literal: Shu knew this was not Jingren's old intention and also feared the High Ancestor's command; he urgently asked leave but was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Shu knew this was not Jingren's wish and feared going against the High Ancestor's summons; he pleaded urgently but was not allowed to refuse.

sentences.zh: 高祖馳遣呼述，須至乃歡。

translations.literal: The High Ancestor sent messengers at speed to summon Shu; only when he arrived did they enjoy themselves.
translations.idiomatic: The High Ancestor sent riders to fetch Shu and would not be merry until he arrived.

sentences.zh: 及景仁有疾，述盡心營視，湯藥飲食，必嘗而後進，不解帶、不盥櫛者累旬，景仁深懷感愧。

translations.literal: When Jingren fell ill Shu devoted his heart to tending him; for decoctions, medicines, food, and drink he always tasted them before presenting them; for many ten-day periods he did not loosen his belt or wash and comb—Jingren deeply felt gratitude and shame.
translations.idiomatic: When Jingren fell ill Shu nursed him devotedly, tasting every medicine and meal before serving it; for weeks he did not undress or wash, and Jingren was deeply moved and ashamed.

sentences.zh: 轉太尉參軍，從征司馬休之，封吉陽縣五等侯。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Retainer of the Grand Commandant, followed the campaign against Sima Xiuzhi, and was enfeoffed as Marquis of the Fifth Rank of Jiyang County.
translations.idiomatic: He became retainer to the Grand Commandant, joined the campaign against Sima Xiuzhi, and was enfeoffed as fifth-rank marquis of Jiyang County.

sentences.zh: 世子征虜參軍，轉主簿，宋臺尚書祠部郎，世子中軍主簿，轉太子中舍人，出補長沙內史，有惠政。

translations.literal: Heir Campaign against Captives Retainer, transferred to Chief Clerk, Song Tower Gentleman of the Ministry of Rites, Heir Center Army Chief Clerk, transferred to Attendant of the Heir Apparent's Center, went out and was supplemented as Interior Minister of Changsha, and had benevolent governance.
translations.idiomatic: He served as retainer in the heir's campaign-against-captives office, then chief clerk, gentleman's post in the Ministry of Rites on the Song Tower staff, chief clerk of the heir's center army, then attendant in the heir's palace; as administrator of Changsha he governed with kindness.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二年，徵拜中書侍郎。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yuanjia he was summoned and appointed Gentleman Attendant of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yuanjia he was summoned to be Gentleman Attendant of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 明年，出為武陵太守，彭城王義康驃騎長史，領南郡太守。

translations.literal: The next year he went out as Administrator of Wuling, Chief Clerk of Rapid Cavalry to the Prince of Pengcheng Yikang, holding concurrently the post of Administrator of Nanjun.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he became administrator of Wuling, chief clerk of Rapid Cavalry to Prince Yikang of Pengcheng, and concurrently administrator of Nanjun.

sentences.zh: 先是，述從兄曜為義康長史，喪官，述代之。

translations.literal: Earlier Shu's father's elder brother's son Yao had been Yikang's Chief Clerk; when he left office Shu replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: Shu's cousin Yao had previously been Yikang's chief clerk; when Yao left office Shu replaced him.

sentences.zh: 太祖與義康書曰：「今以謝述代曜。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizu wrote to Yikang, saying: "I now replace Yao with Xie Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizu wrote Yikang: "I am replacing Yao with Xie Shu.

sentences.zh: 其才應詳練，著於歷職，故以佐汝。

translations.literal: His talent should be thorough and practiced, manifest in his successive offices—therefore I use him to assist you.
translations.idiomatic: His abilities are proven and thorough, demonstrated in every post he has held—that is why I send him to assist you.

sentences.zh: 汝始親庶務，而任重事殷，宜寄懷群賢，以盡弼諧之美，想自得之，不俟吾言也。

translations.literal: You are just beginning to attend personally to the numerous affairs, while your burden is heavy and business abundant—you should entrust your heart to the assembled worthies to exhaust the beauty of harmonious assistance; I think you will grasp this yourself and need not wait for my words.
translations.idiomatic: You are new to daily governance and the burden is heavy; rely on men of talent to govern well—I expect you will understand this without my saying more.

sentences.zh: 」義康入相，述又為司徒左長史，轉左衛將軍。

translations.literal: " When Yikang entered the chancellorship Shu again served as Left Chief Clerk of the Minister of Education and was transferred to Left Guard General.
translations.idiomatic: " When Yikang became chief minister Shu again served as left chief clerk of the Minister of Education, then left guard general.

sentences.zh: 蒞官清約，私無宅舍。

translations.literal: When he took office he was pure and sparing; privately he had no house or dwelling.
translations.idiomatic: In office he was austere and frugal and owned no private residence.

sentences.zh: 義康遇之甚厚。

translations.literal: Yikang treated him very generously.
translations.idiomatic: Yikang treated him with great favor.

sentences.zh: 尚書僕射殷景仁、領軍將軍劉湛並與述為異常之交。

translations.literal: Vice Director of the Secretariat Yin Jingren and General of the Palace Guard Liu Zhan both had with Shu a friendship outside the ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director Yin Jingren and General of the Palace Guard Liu Zhan were both unusually close to him.

sentences.zh: 美風姿，善舉止，湛每謂人曰：「我見謝道兒，未嘗足。

translations.literal: Fine in bearing and appearance, skilled in deportment—Zhan often said to people: "When I see Xie Daor'er I never have my fill.
translations.idiomatic: Handsome in bearing and graceful in manner, Zhan often said, "I never tire of looking at Xie Daor'er.

sentences.zh: 」道兒，述小字也。

translations.literal: " Daor'er was Shu's childhood name.
translations.idiomatic: " Daor'er was Shu's childhood name.

sentences.zh: 雍州刺史張邵以黷貨下廷尉，將致大辟，述上表陳邵先朝舊勳，宜蒙優貸，太祖手詔酬納焉。

translations.literal: Inspector of Yong Province Zhang Shao for corrupt taking of goods was sent down to the Court Commandant and was about to suffer the great execution; Shu submitted a memorial stating Shao's old merit in the former court and that he should receive generous leniency; Emperor Taizu by hand rescript answered and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shao, inspector of Yong Province, was sent to the court commandant for corruption and faced execution; Shu memorialized that Shao's service to the former dynasty merited clemency, and Emperor Taizu personally approved his petition.

sentences.zh: 述語子綜曰：「主上矜邵夙誠，將加曲恕，吾所啟謬會，故特見酬納耳。

translations.literal: Shu told his son Zong, saying: "The sovereign took pity on Shao's old sincerity and was about to grant exceptional pardon; my memorial was a mistaken coincidence, and therefore it was specially answered and accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Shu told his son Zong, "The emperor meant to pardon Shao out of regard for his long service; my memorial merely happened to coincide, which is why he answered it so graciously.

sentences.zh: 若此疏跡宣佈，則為侵奪主恩，不可之大者也。

translations.literal: If this memorial's trace were promulgated, it would be encroaching upon and seizing the sovereign's grace—the greatest of things not to be done.
translations.idiomatic: If word of this memorial spread it would look as if I had stolen the emperor's favor—a thing that must never be done.

sentences.zh: 」使綜對前焚之。

translations.literal: " He had Zong face him and burn it.
translations.idiomatic: " He had Zong burn it before him.

sentences.zh: 太祖後謂邵曰：「卿之獲免，謝述有力焉」。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizu later said to Shao: "Your obtaining pardon—Xie Shu had power in it."
translations.idiomatic: Later Emperor Taizu told Shao, "You owe your pardon in large part to Xie Shu."

sentences.zh: 述有心虛疾，性理時或乖謬。

translations.literal: Shu had an illness of cardiac vacuity; his temperament and reasoning at times were contrary and aberrant.
translations.idiomatic: Shu suffered from a weak heart, and his temper and judgment sometimes failed him.

sentences.zh: 除吳郡太守，以疾不之官。

translations.literal: He was appointed Administrator of Wu Commandery but because of illness did not go to office.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed administrator of Wu Commandery but did not take up the post because of illness.

sentences.zh: 病差，補吳興太守。

translations.literal: When his illness improved he was supplemented as Administrator of Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: When he recovered he was appointed administrator of Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 在郡清省，為吏民所懷。

translations.literal: In the commandery he was pure and sparing and was cherished by officials and people.
translations.idiomatic: In office he was frugal and upright and won the affection of officials and people alike.

sentences.zh: 十二年，卒，時年四十六。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he died, aged forty-six at the time.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he died, aged forty-six.

sentences.zh: 喪還京師，未至數十里，殷景仁、劉湛同乘迎赴，望船流涕。

translations.literal: When the coffin returned to the capital, not yet having reached several tens of li, Yin Jingren and Liu Zhan rode together to meet and go forward; seeing the boat they shed tears.
translations.idiomatic: As the funeral procession neared the capital, still several tens of li away, Yin Jingren and Liu Zhan rode out together to meet it and wept at the sight of the boat.

sentences.zh: 十七年，劉湛誅，義康外鎮，將行，歎曰：「謝述唯勸吾退，劉湛唯勸吾進，今述亡而湛存，吾所以得罪也。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year Liu Zhan was executed; Yikang was sent out to garrison abroad; about to depart he sighed, saying: "Xie Shu only urged me to withdraw; Liu Zhan only urged me to advance—now Shu is dead and Zhan lives; that is why I have offended.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year, after Liu Zhan was executed, Yikang was posted to the provinces; as he was leaving he sighed, "Shu alone urged me to step back and Zhan alone urged me forward—now Shu is dead and Zhan alive; that is how I came to ruin.

sentences.zh: 」太祖亦曰：「謝述若存，義康必不至此。」

translations.literal: " Emperor Taizu also said: "If Xie Shu were alive, Yikang would surely not have come to this."
translations.idiomatic: " Emperor Taizu also said, "Had Shu lived, Yikang would never have come to this pass."

sentences.zh: 三子：綜、約、緯。

translations.literal: Three sons: Zong, Yue, and Wei.
translations.idiomatic: He had three sons: Zong, Yue, and Wei.

sentences.zh: 綜有才藝，善隸書，為太子中舍人，與舅范曄謀反，伏誅。

translations.literal: Zong had literary and artistic talent, was skilled at clerical script, served as Attendant of the Heir Apparent's Center, joined with his maternal uncle Fan Ye in plotting rebellion, and was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Zong was talented in the arts and skilled in clerical script; he served as attendant in the heir's palace, conspired with his uncle Fan Ye to rebel, and was executed.

sentences.zh: 約亦坐死。

translations.literal: Yue also was put to death by association.
translations.idiomatic: Yue was also executed on account of the crime.

sentences.zh: 緯尚太祖第五女長城公主，素為約所憎，免死，徙廣州。

translations.literal: Wei had married Emperor Taizu's fifth daughter, Princess Changcheng; he had long been hated by Yue, was spared death, and was banished to Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wei had married Emperor Taizu's fifth daughter, Princess Changcheng; long hated by Yue, he was spared execution and banished to Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 孝建中，還京師。

translations.literal: During Xiaojian he returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xiaojian era he returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 方雅有父風。

translations.literal: Fang was refined and had his father's manner.
translations.idiomatic: Fang was refined and bore his father's manner.

sentences.zh: 太宗泰始中，至正員郎中。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Taizong in the Taishi era he reached Regular Attendant Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Taizong in the Taishi era he rose to regular attendant gentleman.

sentences.zh: 袁湛，字士深，陳郡陽夏人也。

translations.literal: Yuan Zhan, courtesy name Shishen, was a native of Yangxia in Chen Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Zhan, styled Shishen, came from Yangxia in Chen Commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖耽，晉歷陽太守。

translations.literal: His grandfather Dan was Administrator of Liyang under Jin.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Dan had been administrator of Liyang under Jin.

sentences.zh: 父質，琅邪內史，並知名。

translations.literal: His father Zhi was Interior Minister of Langye; both were well known.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhi was interior minister of Langye; both were well known.

sentences.zh: 湛少為從外祖謝安所知，以其兄子玄之女妻之。

translations.literal: In youth Zhan won recognition from his maternal uncle's uncle Xie An, who gave him in marriage the daughter of his elder brother's son Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth Zhan won Xie An's notice; An gave him the daughter of his nephew Xuan in marriage.

sentences.zh: 初為衛軍行參軍，員外散騎，通直正員郎，中軍功曹，桓玄太尉參軍事。

translations.literal: At first he served as Acting Retainer of the Guard Army, Extraordinary Attendant Cavalier-in-Ordinary, Regular Attendant of Direct Communication, Merit Officer of the Center Army, and Staff Officer to Huan Xuan's Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: He first served as acting retainer of the Guard Army, extraordinary attendant cavalier-in-ordinary, regular attendant of direct communication, merit officer of the center army, and staff officer to Huan Xuan as Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 入為中書黃門侍郎，出補桓脩撫軍長史。

translations.literal: He entered service as Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate in the Secretariat, then went out and was supplemented as Chief Clerk to Huan Xiu's Pacifying Army.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the Secretariat as attendant gentleman of the yellow gate, then went out as chief clerk to Huan Xiu's Pacifying Army.

sentences.zh: 義旗建，高祖以為鎮軍諮議參軍。

translations.literal: When the righteous banner was raised, the High Ancestor made him Advising Staff Officer of the Pacification Army.
translations.idiomatic: When the righteous banner was raised, the High Ancestor made him advising staff officer of the Pacification Army.

sentences.zh: 明年，轉尚書吏部郎，司徒左長史，侍中。

translations.literal: The next year he was transferred to Director of the Ministry of the Civil Service in the Secretariat, Left Chief Clerk to the Minister of Education, and Attendant at Court.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he became director of the Ministry of the Civil Service, left chief clerk to the Minister of Education, and attendant at court.

sentences.zh: 以從征功，封晉寧縣五等男。

translations.literal: For his service on campaign he was enfeoffed as Baron of the Fifth Rank of Jinning County.
translations.idiomatic: For his service on campaign he was enfeoffed as fifth-rank baron of Jinning County.

sentences.zh: 出為高祖太尉長史，遷左民尚書，徙掌吏部。

translations.literal: He went out as Chief Clerk to the High Ancestor's Grand Commandant, was promoted to Director of the Left House, and was transferred to take charge of the Ministry of the Civil Service.
translations.idiomatic: He went out as chief clerk to the High Ancestor's Grand Commandant, was promoted director of the Left House, and was put in charge of the Ministry of the Civil Service.

sentences.zh: 出為吳興太守，秩中二千石，蒞政和理，為吏民所稱。

translations.literal: He went out as Administrator of Wuxing, rank middle two-thousand-dan; his governance was harmonious and orderly, and officials and people praised him.
translations.idiomatic: As administrator of Wuxing, rank middle two-thousand-dan, he governed harmoniously and won praise from officials and people alike.

sentences.zh: 入補中書令，又出為吳國內史，秩中二千石。

translations.literal: He entered and was supplemented as Director of the Secretariat, then went out again as Interior Minister of Wu, rank middle two-thousand-dan.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as director of the Secretariat, then sent out again as interior minister of Wu with rank middle two-thousand-dan.

sentences.zh: 義熙十二年，轉尚書右僕射、本州大中正。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Yixi he was transferred to Vice Director of the Right in the Secretariat and Rectifier of Standards for his native province.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of Yixi he became vice director of the right in the Secretariat and rectifier of standards for his native province.

sentences.zh: 時高祖北伐，湛兼太尉，與兼司空、散騎常侍、尚書范泰奉九命禮物，拜授高祖。

translations.literal: At that time the High Ancestor was on the northern campaign; Zhan served concurrently as Grand Commandant and, with Acting Minister of Works, Regular Attendant Cavalier-in-Ordinary, and Secretariat Director Fan Tai, presented the nine accoutrements of investiture and conferred them upon the High Ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: While the High Ancestor was on his northern campaign, Zhan served concurrently as Grand Commandant and, with Fan Tai, acting Minister of Works, regular attendant cavalier-in-ordinary, and director of the Secretariat, presented the nine accoutrements of investiture to the High Ancestor.

sentences.zh: 高祖沖讓，湛等隨軍至洛陽，住柏谷塢。

translations.literal: The High Ancestor declined with humility; Zhan and the others followed the army to Luoyang and lodged at Baigu Stockade.
translations.idiomatic: The High Ancestor modestly declined; Zhan and the others followed the army to Luoyang and stayed at Baigu Stockade.

sentences.zh: 泰議受使未畢，不拜晉帝陵，湛獨至五陵致敬，時人美之。

translations.literal: Tai argued that his mission was not yet complete and did not visit the Jin imperial tombs; Zhan alone went to the Five Imperial Tombs to pay respects, and people of the time praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Tai held that his mission was incomplete and refused to visit the Jin imperial tombs; Zhan alone went to the Five Imperial Tombs to pay respects, and contemporaries praised him.

sentences.zh: 子淳，淳子桓卒。

translations.literal: His son was Chun; Chun's son Huan died young.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Chun; Chun's son Huan died young.

sentences.zh: 湛弟豹，字士蔚，亦為謝安所知，好學博聞，多覽典籍。

translations.literal: Zhan's younger brother Bao, courtesy name Shiwei, was also recognized by Xie An; he loved learning, was broadly informed, and read many classics and records.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan's younger brother Bao, styled Shiwei, also won Xie An's notice; he loved learning, was widely read, and pored over the classics.

sentences.zh: 初為著作佐郎，衛軍桓謙記室參軍。

translations.literal: At first he served as Assistant Gentleman of the Directorate of Writing and Recording Staff Officer to Huan Qian's Guard Army.
translations.idiomatic: He first served as assistant gentleman of the Directorate of Writing and recording staff officer to Huan Qian's Guard Army.

sentences.zh: 大將軍武陵王遵承制，復為記室參軍。

translations.literal: When Grand General Prince Zun of Wuling assumed imperial authority, Bao again became Recording Staff Officer.
translations.idiomatic: When Grand General Prince Zun of Wuling assumed imperial authority, Bao again became recording staff officer.

sentences.zh: 其年，丹陽尹孟昶以為建威司馬。

translations.literal: That year the Governor of Danyang Meng Chang made him Establishing-Might Major.
translations.idiomatic: That year the governor of Danyang Meng Chang made him major of the army that establishes might.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，轉司徒左西屬，遷劉毅撫軍諮議參軍，領記室。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was transferred to Left Western Attendant under the Minister of Education, then moved to Advising Staff Officer to Liu Yi's Pacifying Army, concurrently heading the secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year he became left western attendant under the Minister of Education, then advising staff officer to Liu Yi's Pacifying Army, concurrently heading the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 毅時建議大田，豹上議曰：

translations.literal: At that time Yi proposed large-scale state farming; Bao submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yi proposed large-scale state farming, Bao submitted a memorial saying:

sentences.zh: 國因民以為本，民資食以為天，修其業則教興，崇其本則末理，實為治之要道，致化之所階也。

translations.literal: The state takes the people as its foundation; the people take food as their heaven. Cultivate their occupation and instruction rises; honor the root and the branches are ordered. This is truly the essential way of governance and the stair by which transformation is achieved.
translations.idiomatic: The state rests on the people; the people live by grain. Nurture their livelihood and teaching flourishes; strengthen the root and the branches fall into order. This is the essential path of governance and the ladder to transformation.

sentences.zh: 不敦其本，則末業滋章；

translations.literal: If the root is not honored, secondary pursuits grow ever more prominent;
translations.idiomatic: Neglect the root and secondary pursuits multiply;

sentences.zh: 饑寒交湊，則廉恥不立。

translations.literal: when hunger and cold press together, integrity and shame cannot stand.
translations.idiomatic: when hunger and cold press in together, honor and shame collapse.

sentences.zh: 當今接篡偽之末，值凶荒之餘，爭源既開，雕薄彌啟，榮利蕩其正性，賦斂罄其所資，良疇無側趾之耦，比屋有困餧之患，中間多故，日不暇給。

translations.literal: The present age follows upon usurpation and false rule and meets the aftermath of famine and disaster. The springs of contention are already open and ornate frivolity ever more widespread. Glory and profit shake their upright nature; levies and exactions drain what sustains them. Good fields lack a second pair of feet to work them; house after house suffers the distress of hunger. In the interval many troubles arose, and the days allowed no respite.
translations.idiomatic: We stand at the end of usurpation and false rule, in the wake of famine and disaster. Contention is already abroad and frivolity ever more rampant; profit and rank shake men's upright nature, and taxes drain what little they have. Good fields lack hands to work them; house after house knows hunger. Troubles have piled up for years, and there has been no respite.

sentences.zh: 自卷甲卻馬，甫一二年，積弊之黎，難用克振，實仁懷之所矜恤，明教之所爰發也。

translations.literal: Since armor was rolled up and horses withdrawn, only a year or two have passed; the people long burdened by accumulated abuses cannot quickly be restored. This is truly what humane care should pity and enlightened instruction should set in motion.
translations.idiomatic: Since arms were laid aside only a year or two ago, a people long crushed by accumulated abuses cannot quickly be restored. This is precisely what humane rule should pity and enlightened policy should address.

sentences.zh: 然斯業不修，有自來矣。

translations.literal: Yet this enterprise has gone untended for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: Yet this work has long gone neglected.

sentences.zh: 司牧之官，莫或為務，俗吏庸近，猶秉常科，依勸督之故典，迷民情之屢變。
